items.note: The proposal must have a Capabilities section that holds the New/Modified subsections.

sources.quote: - **Capabilities**: Identify which specs will be created or modified:

items.downgrade_reason: The kebab-case rule covers only path segments the change introduces. A reused existing capability path may not be kebab-case, and the engine cannot tell new segments from reused ones.

sources.quote: Each becomes a new `specs/<capability-path>/spec.md`. ... Use kebab-case for path segments you introduce (e.g., `user-auth` or `identity/user-auth`)

items.downgrade_reason: Whether a path follows the project's spec organization is a judgment call. No kind can compare a path's layout convention against openspec/specs.

sources.quote: follow the project's existing spec organization.

items.note: Checking this needs each Modified Capabilities entry mapped to openspec/specs/<path>/spec.md at BASE_SHA. No selector can add that path prefix and suffix, so a cross_ref against base_paths cannot be written.

sources.quote: Use the exact existing path under `openspec/specs/`.
- **Impact**: Affected code, APIs, dependencies, or systems.

items.note: Every openspec show call made in ff to read specs must keep --type spec.

sources.quote: Append `--store "<id>"` to both commands only for a registered standalone store, and keep `--type spec`: a change and a spec sharing a name is otherwise an ambiguous-item error.

items.downgrade_reason: Whether any existing spec is relevant cannot be observed. If none is relevant, no full read is required.

sources.quote: Before deciding what is already covered or what should change, read each relevant spec in full, including scenarios, with `openspec show "<spec-id>" --type spec` (same `--store` rule).

items.note: Every New or Modified capability listed in the proposal has a matching specs/<capability-path>/spec.md. This item also covers schema-006 and schema-012.

sources.quote: Each capability listed here will need a corresponding spec file.

items.downgrade_reason: The skip_specs: true opt-out in the change's .openspec.yaml cannot be expressed as an observable predicate, so a change that legitimately opts out would wrongly fail.

sources.quote: Every change must either declare at least one capability (new or modified) or explicitly opt out of specs: `openspec validate` rejects a change with zero deltas unless the change's `.openspec.yaml` sets `skip_specs: true`.

unitemized.reason: The New Capabilities heading is already compiled from the template. The rule that each new capability becomes a spec file is checked by the schema-020 openspec.capabilities listed_have_specs item. Naming capabilities after durable behavior and choosing a cohesive boundary are semantic judgments.
Whether to include a capability depends on whether spec-level behavior actually changes. That is a semantic judgment no observable predicate captures.
The rule that each modified capability needs a delta spec file is checked by the schema-020 openspec.capabilities listed_have_specs item, which covers both New and Modified capabilities.
This is a permission (Modified Capabilities may be left empty), not an obligation. Nothing to check.
The statement is implicit and informational: bare openspec list shows changes, not specs. Running it is not prohibited, and relying on it for a capability inventory cannot be observed.
Detecting a near-duplicate capability name needs fuzzy semantic comparison against existing spec paths. No kind expresses that.
